Score a dart by how far from the centre of the target it lands.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/darts) (MIT). Listed under [Games & Simulation](/examples/?subject=games-and-simulation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: darts.nomi
/// The points a dart landing at `x`, `y` scores on a target centred on the
/// origin: 10 inside radius 1, 5 inside radius 5, 1 inside radius 10, and
/// nothing outside. A dart on a circle's edge counts as inside it.
pub fn score(x: Float, y: Float) -> Int {
    distance_squared = x * x + y * y

    case distance_squared {
        d when d <= 1.0 -> 10
        d when d <= 25.0 -> 5
        d when d <= 100.0 -> 1
        _ -> 0
    }
}

// FILE: darts_test.nomi
import darts

test "scores a toss" {
    cases = [
        #("Missed target", #(-9.0, 9.0), 0),
        #("On the outer circle", #(0.0, 10.0), 1),
        #("On the middle circle", #(-5.0, 0.0), 5),
        #("On the inner circle", #(0.0, -1.0), 10),
        #("Exactly on center", #(0.0, 0.0), 10),
        #("Near the center", #(-0.1, -0.1), 10),
        #("Just within the inner circle", #(0.7, 0.7), 10),
        #("Just outside the inner circle", #(0.8, -0.8), 5),
        #("Just within the middle circle", #(-3.5, 3.5), 5),
        #("Just outside the middle circle", #(-3.6, -3.6), 1),
        #("Just within the outer circle", #(-7.0, 7.0), 1),
        #("Just outside the outer circle", #(7.1, -7.1), 0),
        #("Asymmetric position between the inner and middle circles", #(0.5, -4.0), 5),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, #(x, y), expected), description {
        assert darts.score(x, y) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The distance is compared squared, against 1, 25 and 100, so no square root is needed and a dart exactly on a circle (`0, 10`) scores as inside it with no rounding.
- The bands are `case` arms with `when` guards, checked from the inside out. An `if`/`else if` ladder was the other form; the arms line up the radii and their points.
- `score` takes two `Float`s and returns an `Int`. The canonical inputs that are whole numbers are written `9.0` in the tests, since an `Int` literal is not a `Float`.
- The 13 cases are one `subtests` table whose middle column is the `#(x, y)` point.
